questions.question: How many degrees of arc does one hour position on a clock face correspond to?
questions.rationale: A full circle (360°) is divided across 12 hour positions: 360° / 12 = 30° per hour position.

questions.question: The minute hand sweeps 360° in 60 minutes. How many degrees does it move per minute?
questions.rationale: 360° / 60 minutes = 6° per minute, so at 20 minutes past the hour the minute hand sits at 6 × 20 = 120°.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at 3:20, using D = |30H − 5.5M|?
questions.rationale: D = |30(3) − 5.5(20)| = |90 − 110| = 20°, and 20° is already the smaller of the two possible angles.

questions.question: Why is it a mistake to assume the hour hand sits exactly on the '3' at 3:30?
options: The hour hand only moves once every hour
The hour hand moves continuously between hour marks as minutes pass (0.5° per minute)
Clocks with hour hands are always analog and inaccurate
The minute hand also stays fixed on the hour marks
questions.rationale: The hour hand moves continuously, 0.5° per minute — at 3:30, θ_h = 30(3) + 0.5(30) = 105°, not exactly on the 3 (90°).
